presets.title: Audit the level's lighting before you change it
presets.summary: Read the sun, sky, fog, post process, local lights and renderer settings, capture the view, and score it against the lighting-artist bar.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

presets.prompt:
Audit the lighting of {{level}} from the camera `{{camera}}` without changing anything. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_memory_recall "lighting" for earlier decisions and match studies about this level.
2. hyper_lighting_inspect with CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`, MaxLocalLights 64, MaxMaterials 12. Summarise: sun or Blueprint sky, sky light, fog, atmosphere, clouds, post process settings that differ from the defaults, local lights in view, whether exposure is locked, and the rendering list (gi_method, reflection_method, lumen_tracing, megalights, static_lighting).
3. hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (source viewport if that camera does not exist), 1280 x 720.
4. Judge the frame against the lighting-artist bar from the capture's metrics and what you see.
Report a PASS/FAIL/WARN table: exposure locked (WARN if not: captures then measure the eye adapting, not the light), LuminanceP95 < 0.95, LuminanceP5 > 0.02, one clear key light direction, no more than 4 shadow-casting local lights overlapping in view, materials with notes (list them), and the frame's ColorTemperatureK with the time of day it suggests. Then the capture on its own line as ![{{camera}}](absolute path), and the three changes you would make first, each naming the lighting plan op that would make it (such as set_sun pitch or set_fog density).

presets.title: Lock exposure and calibrate it to mid-grey
presets.summary: Turn off auto exposure at an EV100 that puts the frame's median brightness near 18%, so later lighting changes can be measured fairly.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

placeholders.name: start_ev
placeholders.label: Starting EV100
placeholders.hint: About 15 noon sun, 12 overcast, 8 bright interior, 4 dim interior, -2 moonlight

presets.prompt:
Lock the exposure of {{level}} so captures measure the light, not the eye adapting. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`): note bExposureLocked, whether a Blueprint sky such as Ultra Dynamic Sky is present (its lights are not physical, so EV100 often sits between -3 and 3), and the revision.
2. hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false) with one lock_exposure op at EV100 {{start_ev}}. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait with that OperationId.
3. hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (viewport if it does not exist) and read LuminanceP50. Set the next EV100 to the current one plus log2(P50 / {{target_p50}}) and lock again, with a fresh inspect revision and OperationId. Repeat until P50 is within 20% of {{target_p50}}, at most 5 times.
4. hyper_memory_remember the result, titled with the fact itself, such as "<level> locks at EV100 N from <camera>".
Report a PASS/FAIL table: exposure locked, final EV100, P50 within 20% of {{target_p50}}, LuminanceP95 < 0.95, LuminanceP5 > 0.02, memory saved. Then the first and last captures, each on its own line as ![EV100 ...](absolute path). Leave the level unsaved.

presets.title: Measure how far the view is from a reference image
presets.summary: Compare the current view with a reference by brightness, contrast, colour temperature and saturation, and list the changes that would close the gap.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

presets.prompt:
Tell me how far {{level}} is from the look in `{{reference}}` and what to change first. Change nothing. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. Open the reference and describe its key light, shadows, palette and contrast in two sentences.
2. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`): if bExposureLocked is false, say that brightness numbers measure auto exposure and mark them WARN.
3. hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (viewport if it does not exist), at the reference's aspect ratio.
4. hyper_lighting_compare with ReferenceImagePath `{{reference}}` and CurrentImagePath the capture: ExposureDeltaEV, ColorTemperatureDeltaK, ContrastRatioDelta, SaturationDelta, HistogramDistance and Suggestions.
5. hyper_image_compare (mode look, Grid 4) of the capture against the reference: Score, PaletteScore, ToneScore, LayoutScore, DetailScore and the three worst regions.
Report a table of each measure (reference, current, delta), PASS when |ExposureDeltaEV| <= 0.5, |ColorTemperatureDeltaK| <= 500, |ContrastRatioDelta| <= 15% of the reference's ContrastRatio and |SaturationDelta| <= 0.1, else FAIL. Then the score, the side-by-side on its own line as ![side by side](absolute path), and the first three changes in order, each naming the lighting plan op that would make it (such as set_sun temperature or set_post_process saturation).

presets.title: Capture a four-angle look-dev sheet of a prop
presets.summary: Frame the selected prop from four sides at one distance under the level's light, and list the materials it shows, for art review.
presets.prompt:
Make a look-dev sheet of {{selected_actor}} for art review. Change nothing in the level. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_scene_inspect (scope selected) for its location; treat it as about {{size_cm}} cm across unless its scale says otherwise.
2. hyper_capture_view four times with source transform: {{distance_cm}} cm from its centre at yaw 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, {{height_cm}} cm above its centre, rotated to look at it, FovDegrees {{fov}}, 1024 x 1024, Label lookdev_<actor label> (letters, digits, - and _ only). Keep bSettle on.
3. hyper_lighting_inspect (MaxMaterials 24): if the prop is in the inspected view, list the materials it shows, their parameters and notes.
Report a PASS/FAIL table with one row per capture: the prop fills 40-80% of the frame (adjust the distance once if not), LuminanceP95 < 0.95, LuminanceP5 > 0.02, bShadersStillCompiling false. Then the four captures, each on its own line as ![yaw ...](absolute path), and any material notes worth fixing.

presets.title: Let light through blockout foliage and glass
presets.summary: Stop the selected blockout shapes that stand in for leaves, cloth or glass from casting solid shadows, and show the before and after.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

presets.prompt:
These blockout shapes stand in for foliage, cloth or glass and should not cast solid shadows yet:
{{selected_actors}}
If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`) for the revision, and note whether exposure is locked.
2. hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (viewport if it does not exist), Label before_shadows.
3. One hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false) with one set_actor_shadow per actor above: empty property (all its meshes), value false. Touch no other actor. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait with that OperationId.
4. hyper_capture_view again from the same camera, Label after_shadows.
Report a PASS/FAIL table: one row per actor (shadow off), ShadowFraction before -> after (it should fall), and the plan's op count equal to the number of actors (nothing else changed). Then the before and after captures, each on its own line. Remind me that set_actor_shadow with value true puts each shadow back when final art arrives.

presets.summary: Set a low warm sun, softer sky fill, warm haze and a gentle grade at a locked exposure, and prove the frame is warm without clipping.

placeholders.hint: Pick so the sun rakes across the main view

presets.prompt:
Light {{level}} for golden hour, seen from `{{camera}}`. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`). If a Blueprint sky such as Ultra Dynamic Sky owns the sun, use set_sky_system (Time of Day about 1800, Sun Yaw) instead of set_sun, set_sky_light, set_fog and set_sky_atmosphere, and say so. hyper_capture_view (source camera, viewport if it does not exist) as the before frame.
2. One hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false): lock_exposure {{ev100}}; set_sun pitch {{sun_pitch}}, yaw {{sun_yaw}}, temperature {{temperature}}, source_angle 1.5; set_sky_light intensity at half its current value; set_fog inscattering_color 1.0,0.75,0.5 and density 1.5 x its inspected value; set_sky_atmosphere MieAnisotropy 0.85; set_post_process shadows_gain 0.95,0.98,1.05 for cooler shadows. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
3. hyper_capture_view again. If LuminanceP50 is outside 0.15-0.25 (the sun may not be in physical lux), lock exposure again at EV100 + log2(P50 / 0.2) in a new plan with a fresh inspect revision, at most 3 times, capturing after each.
Report a PASS/FAIL table: exposure locked (state the final EV100), the frame's ColorTemperatureK below 5000 (warm), LuminanceP50 0.15-0.25, LuminanceP95 < 0.95, LuminanceP5 > 0.02, long shadows (sun pitch between -5 and -15). Then the before and after captures, each on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.prompt:
Make {{level}} a moonlit night for a fantasy village. The selected actors are lanterns:
{{selected_actors}}
If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`, MaxLocalLights 64) and hyper_scene_inspect (scope selected) for each lantern's location. If a Blueprint sky owns the sun, set its night through set_sky_system instead of set_sun and set_sky_light, and say so.
2. One hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false): lock_exposure {{ev100}}; set_sun as the moon: pitch -35, temperature 7500, intensity 0.3; set_sky_light intensity 0.3 x its inspected value with a cool color 0.6,0.7,1.0; for each lantern, add_light point labelled `Lantern_Light_<n>` at its location plus {{lift_cm}} cm up, then set_light temperature {{lantern_k}}, attenuation_radius {{radius_cm}}, source_radius 8, and cast_shadows true only for the 4 nearest the camera (false for the rest). If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
3. hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (viewport if it does not exist). Adjust lantern intensity by ratios (x2 or /2) if the pools clip or vanish, one plan per change, each with a fresh inspect revision.
Report a PASS/FAIL table: one light per lantern, LuminanceP50 between 0.04 and 0.15 (night), LuminanceP95 < 0.95 (lanterns not clipping), at most 4 shadow-casting lantern lights, and WARN if the frame's ColorTemperatureK is below 4000 (lanterns overpowering the moon). Then the capture on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.title: Turn the sky stormy and overcast
presets.summary: Add heavy volumetric clouds, soften and cool the sun, thicken the fog and mute the grade, then prove the frame reads as overcast.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

placeholders.name: saturation
placeholders.label: Post-process saturation
placeholders.hint: 1 is unchanged; lower mutes colour

presets.prompt:
Make {{level}} a stormy overcast day, seen from `{{camera}}`. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`): clouds, fog and the revision. With a Blueprint sky, use set_sky_system (Cloud Coverage, Fog) instead of set_clouds, set_sun, set_sky_light and set_fog, and say so; with Ultra Dynamic Weather, set the weather there. hyper_capture_view (source camera, viewport if it does not exist) as the before frame.
2. One hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false): lock_exposure 12; set_clouds material:Cloud_GlobalCoverage {{coverage}} and material:Cloud_GlobalDensity 1.5 x its inspected value (volumetric clouds are added if the level has none); set_sun temperature 7000, source_angle 10 for soft shadows, intensity a quarter of now; set_sky_light intensity x1.5; set_fog density x3 with inscattering_color 0.55,0.6,0.65; set_post_process saturation {{saturation}} and contrast 0.9. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
3. hyper_capture_view again with bSettle on (clouds take many frames to settle).
Report a PASS/FAIL table: clouds present at coverage {{coverage}}, ContrastRatio lower than before, MeanSaturation lower than before, the frame's ColorTemperatureK above 6000, LuminanceP95 < 0.95, and INFO for bSettleTimedOut (moving clouds) and for the cloud material instance's path under /Game/HyperAI/Clouds/. Then the before and after captures, each on its own line.

presets.title: Add god rays through a forest canopy
presets.summary: Turn on volumetric fog and sun scattering with light-shaft bloom so sunbeams cut through the trees, and prove the beams show without washing out the frame.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

placeholders.name: ev100
placeholders.label: Locked EV100
placeholders.hint: About 15 noon sun, 12 overcast, 8 bright interior, 4 dim interior, -2 moonlight

presets.prompt:
Add visible sunbeams through the canopy of {{level}}, seen from `{{camera}}`. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`). If a Blueprint sky owns the sun and fog, use its Volumetric Fog variable through set_sky_system and say so. hyper_capture_view (source camera, viewport if it does not exist) as the before frame.
2. One hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false): lock_exposure {{ev100}} if exposure is not locked; set_fog volumetric_fog true, volumetric_scattering_distribution {{anisotropy}} (forward scattering), density {{fog_density}}; set_sun VolumetricScatteringIntensity {{scattering}}, light_shaft_bloom true, BloomScale 0.2, BloomThreshold 4, and pitch between -25 and -45 so beams slant down through gaps in the leaves. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
3. hyper_capture_view again with WarmupFrames 8, since volumetric fog settles slowly. If no beams show, raise VolumetricScatteringIntensity once (x2) in a new plan with a fresh inspect revision, and capture again.
Report a PASS/FAIL table: volumetric fog on, LuminanceP50 up by no more than 30% (beams, not a washed-out frame), LuminanceP95 < 0.95, HighlightFraction below 0.05, and distinct beams visible in the after frame (say where). Then the before and after captures, each on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.prompt:
Give the wide view of {{level}} from `{{camera}}` depth: far ridges fade into haze and mist lies low in the valleys. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`). If a Blueprint sky owns the fog, set its Fog and Dust Amount through set_sky_system instead and say so. hyper_capture_view (source camera, viewport if it does not exist) as the before frame.
2. One hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false): lock_exposure {{ev100}} if exposure is not locked; set_sky_atmosphere mie_scale and rayleigh_scale at 2 x and 1.2 x their inspected values (rayleigh_scale is about 0.033 by default) for aerial perspective; set_fog density {{haze_density}}, height_falloff 0.2, start_distance {{start_cm}}; set_fog SecondFogData (FogDensity={{mist_density}},FogHeightFalloff=0.5,FogHeightOffset={{mist_offset_cm}}) for the valley mist. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
3. hyper_capture_view again from the same camera.
4. hyper_image_compare the after capture against the before in aligned mode, Grid 4, to see which cells changed.
Report a PASS/FAIL table: the cells holding the far ridges brightened and lost detail (DetailRatio below 1), the nearest cells' |BrightenEV| below 0.3, ContrastRatio lower than before, LuminanceP95 < 0.95. Then the before, after and side-by-side images, each on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.title: Set Ultra Dynamic Sky to dawn, noon and dusk
presets.summary: Drive a Blueprint sky's Time of Day through three looks, capture each at a locked exposure, and leave it at the time you choose.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

placeholders.name: ev100
placeholders.label: Starting EV100
placeholders.hint: Blueprint skies often need -3 to 3

presets.prompt:
{{level}} has a Blueprint sky such as Ultra Dynamic Sky. Show me dawn, noon and dusk from `{{camera}}`, then leave it at {{keep}}. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, or hyper_lighting_inspect lists no sky_system record, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`): the sky's variables and its current Time of Day.
2. For each of 600, 1200 and 1800: one hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, fresh ExpectedRevision, bSave false) with set_sky_system Time of Day = that value (empty actor_label), then hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (viewport if it does not exist), Label tod_<time>. If a reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait. Put lock_exposure {{ev100}} in the first plan.
3. This sky's lights are not physical: if the noon frame's LuminanceP50 is outside 0.12-0.25, change EV100 by log2(P50 / 0.18) with lock_exposure and capture noon again. Dawn and dusk may stay darker.
4. Finish with set_sky_system Time of Day {{keep}}, and hyper_memory_remember the EV100 this sky needs once exposure is locked.
Report a PASS/FAIL table, one row per time: LuminanceP50, LuminanceP95 < 0.95, ColorTemperatureK (dawn and dusk warmer than noon). Then rows for the final Time of Day = {{keep}} and the memory saved, and the three captures, each on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.title: Lift crushed shadows without flattening the frame
presets.summary: Open up shadows that go black using source angle, shadow amount, sky occlusion, bounce and local exposure, one lever at a time, keeping contrast.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

placeholders.name: ev100
placeholders.label: EV100 if exposure is unlocked
placeholders.hint: About 15 noon sun, 12 overcast, 8 bright interior, 4 dim interior, -2 moonlight

presets.prompt:
Shadows in {{level}} seen from `{{camera}}` crush to black. Lift them so detail reads, without flattening the frame. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`); if exposure is not locked, lock_exposure at {{ev100}} first in its own plan. hyper_capture_view (source camera, viewport if it does not exist): record LuminanceP5, ShadowFraction and ContrastRatio as the baseline.
2. Apply one lever per hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId and inspect revision each, bDryRun false, bSave false), capturing after each, in this order, and stop once LuminanceP5 >= {{target_p5}}: (a) set_sun source_angle 3 and ShadowAmount 0.85; (b) set_sky_light intensity x1.5, MinOcclusion 0.15, OcclusionTint 0.05,0.06,0.1; (c) set_sun IndirectLightingIntensity 1.3 and set_post_process IndirectLightingIntensity 1.2; (d) set_post_process LocalExposureShadowContrastScale 0.8 and AmbientOcclusionIntensity 0.35; (e) last, set_post_process shadows_gain 1.1,1.1,1.15. Never use LumenDiffuseColorBoost or LumenSkylightLeaking. If a reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
Report a table with one row per lever applied: LuminanceP5, ShadowFraction and ContrastRatio after it. Then PASS/FAIL: LuminanceP5 >= {{target_p5}}, ContrastRatio still >= {{min_contrast}}, LuminanceP95 < 0.95. Then the baseline and final captures, each on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.title: Grade the level to a reference with a fitted LUT
presets.summary: Fit a colour-grading LUT that takes the current view to a reference's colours, apply it only if it scores higher, and soften it to taste.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

placeholders.name: mode
placeholders.label: Compare mode (look or aligned)
placeholders.hint: aligned only when the reference frames the same view

presets.prompt:
Grade {{level}} toward the colours of `{{reference}}`, as a colourist would, once the light is already close. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`): exposure must be locked; if it is not, say so and stop, since a LUT fitted to auto exposure is wrong.
2. hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (viewport if it does not exist), then hyper_image_compare against the reference (mode {{mode}}, SessionId {{session}}, Note "before LUT", bFitLut true). Read Score, LutScore, LutPath and LutSideBySidePath, and open the side-by-side.
3. Only if LutScore beats Score by at least 2 points: one hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision from a fresh inspect, bSave false) with set_post_process color_grading_lut <LutPath>, then set_post_process ColorGradingIntensity {{intensity}}. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait. Otherwise stop and say the grade is not the gap.
4. hyper_capture_view again and hyper_image_compare in the same session, with a Note naming the LUT and intensity.
Report a PASS/FAIL table: exposure locked, score before -> after, after within 3 points of LutScore or better, LuminanceP95 < 0.95, and the LUT texture's path under /Game/HyperAI/LUTs/. Then the before and after side-by-sides, each on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.title: Fix surfaces that take light wrongly, in the level only
presets.summary: Find materials in view whose base colour, metallic or specular break physical ranges and correct them on the level's own instances, never the project's.

placeholders.name: camera
placeholders.label: Camera label
placeholders.hint: The view to judge; the level viewport is used if no camera has this label

presets.prompt:
Make the surfaces in view of `{{camera}}` in {{level}} take light like real materials, without changing any project material. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`, MaxMaterials {{max_materials}}): each material's viewShare, parameters and notes (non-metal base colour outside 0.02-0.81, metallic between 0 and 1, specular far from 0.5, unlit surfaces, roughness above lumen_max_roughness_to_trace where the surface should mirror). hyper_capture_view as the before frame.
2. For each material with a note a parameter can fix, largest viewShare first: one hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId and inspect revision, bDryRun false, bSave false) with set_material_parameter on an actor showing it, property [slot:<n>/]<parameter>, using physical values: metallic 0 or 1, specular 0.5 (water 0.255), non-metal base colour inside 0.02-0.81. Use set_actor_material_parameter only when one actor must differ from the rest. If a value is fixed inside the material or is a static switch, list it for the material tools instead. If a reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
3. hyper_lighting_inspect and hyper_capture_view again.
Report a table: material, note, parameter, before -> after, PASS/FAIL (note gone). Then PASS/FAIL rows: no project material changed (only instances under /Game/HyperAI/LookDev/), LuminanceP95 < 0.95. Then the before and after captures, each on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

1. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`, MaxLocalLights 64) for the revision and the lights already there; hyper_scene_inspect (scope selected) for each marker's location.

One hyper_lighting_apply_plan (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false): lock_exposure {{ev100}}; set_sky_light intensity 0.1 so unlit areas fall to near black; for each marker, add_light spot labelled `Pool_<n>` {{height_cm}} cm above its location, then set_light aim_at the marker's location below it, outer_cone_angle {{cone}}, inner_cone_angle half of that, temperature {{temperature}}, attenuation_radius {{radius_cm}}, volumetric_scattering 2; set_fog volumetric_fog true. Switch off (set_light enabled false) only these existing lights: {{lights_off}}. If the reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait.
3. hyper_capture_view with source camera `{{camera}}` (viewport if it does not exist).
Report a PASS/FAIL table: one spot per marker, ShadowFraction between 0.35 and 0.75, ContrastRatio >= 20, LuminanceP95 < 0.95, at most 4 shadow-casting lights overlapping. Then the capture on its own line. Leave the level unsaved.

presets.prompt:
Match the lighting of {{level}} seen from `{{camera}}` to `{{reference}}`, following the image-match skill. If the lighting_lookdev pack is unavailable, say so and stop.
1. Open the reference and say what makes the look: time of day, key light, palette, contrast, air. hyper_memory_recall "match" for earlier studies of this level.
2. hyper_lighting_inspect (CameraActorLabel `{{camera}}`); if the camera does not exist, say so and use the viewport. hyper_lighting_apply_plan with lock_exposure at a fitting EV100 (fresh OperationId, bDryRun false, ExpectedRevision, bSave false).
3. Loop at most {{max_iterations}} times: hyper_capture_view of the camera; hyper_image_compare (mode {{mode}}, TargetScore {{target}}, SessionId {{session}}, a Note naming the values just changed); open the side-by-side; then one hyper_lighting_apply_plan with one lever or one coherent group (set_sun angle and temperature, set_sky_light, set_fog, set_sky_atmosphere, set_post_process, set_light, or set_sky_system for a Blueprint sky), with a fresh OperationId and revision each time. If a reply is still pending, hyper_operation_wait. On bPlateau, switch lever category. Stop on bMatched.
4. When the light is close, compare once with bFitLut true, and apply set_post_process color_grading_lut <LutPath> only if LutScore beats the score.
5. hyper_memory_remember one lasting fact you learned, such as the EV100 this level needs.
Report a table of iterations (score and note), then PASS/FAIL: best score >= {{target}}, exposure locked, level unsaved. Then the best side-by-side on its own line as ![best](absolute path).
